hard: output: 'export' — NO server-side code, NO API routes, NO getServerSideProps

NO amber as a primary action color — orange only for buttons/links/active states
NO border-l-4 side-stripe on active/selected states — use full border

compatibility: Must work on iOS Safari, Android Chrome, desktop browsers (fetch + FormData/JSON)

security_requirements: Contact form submissions are anonymous/unauthenticated (no user session required)
No sensitive data collected (name, email, app version are all optional)

gotchas.text: Next 16 uses 'use client' directive for interactive components. Contact.tsx needs it because it uses useState for form state, loading, success, error.
The Navbar has separate code paths for FAQ (anchor scroll on homepage vs. page navigation elsewhere). Contact is simpler — always navigates to /contact, no anchor behavior needed.
Google Apps Script doPost(e) receives the POST body as e.postData.contents (a string). Must JSON.parse() it. The response format must include ContentService.MimeType.JSON.
Tailwind v4 auto-generates utility classes from @theme tokens. --color-surface-50 becomes bg-surface-50, border-surface-50, etc. Do not use theme() or @apply.

security_considerations.concern: Webhook URL is a hardcoded constant in the public JS bundle. This is acceptable for a Google Sheets webhook (the URL alone doesn't grant write access without the Apps Script). But it means the URL is visible to anyone who inspects the page source.
Form input is sent directly to Google Sheets. No XSS risk in the sheet itself, but the Apps Script should not eval() user input. The provided doPost code only appends rows.

testing_patterns.framework: Manual E2E testing via gem-browser-tester (no Jest/Cypress configured)
mock_patterns: N/A — testing against real build output, not mocked

domain_context.error_handling: Client-side try/catch around fetch. Show error message with retry prompt on failure. Console.warn if webhook URL is still placeholder. Distinguish between validation errors (block submit) and network errors (show error state).
domain_context.data_flow: User fills form → client-side validation → fetch POST JSON to Google Sheets webhook → Apps Script parses JSON → appends row to sheet → returns JSON success/error → UI shows success or error state.

prior_decisions.decision: Use Google Sheets as contact form backend via Apps Script webhook
rationale: Easy for user to review submissions in a spreadsheet

prior_decisions.decision: Standalone /contact page (not a section on the homepage)
rationale: Keeps the homepage focused on product marketing
Better SEO with a focused meta title and description

prior_decisions.decision: Contact link placement: FAQ → Contact → Featured Shelves
rationale: Contact is a utility page — natural to place after FAQ (also a utility page)
Featured Shelves is content — comes after utility links
Matches common SaaS landing page nav conventions
evidence: Best practice for landing page nav ordering

prior_decisions.decision: Webhook URL as constant in Contact.tsx (not a separate config file)
rationale: Minimizes file sprawl for a single constant
User only needs to edit one file to configure the webhook
No module resolution edge cases with static export
evidence: Simplicity over abstraction for a single constant
